title: Employee Names Containing The Letter A
description:
Report the `name` of every employee whose name contains the letter `a` **anywhere**, case-insensitively (not just at the start).

Name the column `name`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE LOWER(name) LIKE '%a%';
hint: A leading and trailing `%` means "anywhere in the string" — anchoring only the start (`'a%'`) or only the end (`'%a'`) would answer a different question.
outputExplanation: Ava, Cara, Dan, Gia and Hal all contain the letter 'a' in their names. Ben, Eve and Finn do not and are excluded.
schemaSql:
CREATE TABLE departments (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  location TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE employees (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  title TEXT,
  salary INTEGER,
  dept_id INTEGER,
  manager_id INTEGER,
  hire_date TEXT
);

tests.name: Department with no employees
Employees with NULL department and NULL salary
Single employee, single department
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Solo','Engineer',100000,1,NULL,'2022-04-01');

tests.name: Duplicate names and same hire dates
Zero and negative salaries, boundary dates
All employees contain the letter 'a'
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'E','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Ada','E',100000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'Ava','E',90000,1,1,'2020-01-01'),(3,'Ana','E',80000,1,1,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: No employees contain the letter 'a'
tests.seedSql:

INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Ben','E',100000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'Cy','E',90000,1,1,'2020-01-01');
